summary: A scholar of religious studies and linguistics, Caquot studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held posts at the EPHE (~1954–1972), University of Strasbourg, University of Paris, and Collège de France (1972–1994).

Working in Indology and religious studies, Couture studied at Laval University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972–1977). He served on the faculty at Laval University from ~1980 to 2010.

Godard worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies after studying at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts. He held posts with DAFA (1923), the Archaeological Service of Iran (~1928–1953), and the University of Tehran (~1934–1949).

A linguist, Martinet studied at ENS, Humboldt University, and the University of Paris/Sorbonne under Joseph Vendryes and Antoine Meillet. His career included posts at EPHE (1938–1946), Columbia University (1947–1955), the University of Paris (~1955–1969), and Paris Descartes (~1969–1977).
A linguist, Mazon was educated at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1898–1904) and Charles University (~1903–1905). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.
Oltramare served as Professor of Latin at the University of Geneva from ~1856 to 1888, where he succeeded Paul Oltramare.

Padoux specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne and under mentors including Louis Renou, Olivier Lacombe, and Swami Lakshman Joo. He held research director posts at CNRS (~1959–1985) and directed Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964).
A scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics, Wedemeyer earned his doctorate under August Conrady (~1910–1916). He later held an academic post at the University of Leipzig.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Rotman studied at CIHTS and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins. He held posts at Smith College (attested 2013–2026) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Krause specializes in Indology and computational fields, having studied at the universities of Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, and Marburg. She held research posts at Leipzig, Marburg, Halle-Wittenberg, Mainz Academy of Sciences and Literature, and the Royal Library of Berlin (2023).

Working in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Howard completed her doctorate at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda. She later served as a professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Manderscheid, a scholar in Tibetology, held academic posts at the Free University of Berlin and as a researcher at the University of Oulu (attested 1998).

Active in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, Sumegi earned her Ph.D. from the University of Ottawa and studied under Nalini Devdas. She served as an assistant professor at Carleton University (attested 2008).
Specializing in religious studies and Sinology, Zito earned her Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1980–1989). She was appointed Associate Professor at New York University in 1999.

Krebs studied philosophy at Freiburg, Oxford, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, and Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held positions at Konstanz, Goethe University Frankfurt (1993–2001), and the University of Basel, where she assumed a chair in 2001.

Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Malinar studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Tübingen. She held teaching posts at the Free University of Berlin, SOAS University of London (~2000–2007), and the University of Zurich (2009).
Brelich specialized in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He completed his studies at Erzsébet University in 1937 and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome from ~1958 to 1977.

An Indologist and linguist, De Gubernatis studied at Turin under Giovanni Flechia and in Berlin under Bopp and Weber. He served as professor at the University of Florence / Istituto di Studi Superiori (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890–1908).

A scholar in Indology and linguistics, Maffei was educated at the Seminario Maggiore Arcivescovile di Trento and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He served as Rector of St Aloysius College (1891–1896) and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.
An Indologist who studied under Carlo Formichi at the University of Pisa, Pizzagalli taught at the University of Pisa (1913), the University of Genoa (1914), and the University of Milan (~1924–1944).
